newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico March CPI 1.24 percent - Banco de Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Mexico March CPI 1.24 percent - Banco de Mexico.

text.p: Mexico's consumer price index rose 1.24 percent in March after rising 1.68 percent in February, the Banco de Mexico said on Wednesday.
Consumer prices had registered a rise of 0.66 percent for the first half of March.
The central bank added that the producer price index rose 0.97 percent in March from the month before, compared to rise of 1.39 percent in February.
A survey of 11 Mexico City brokerages and economists had forecast a rise in consumer prices in March of 1.31 percent.
The central bank said that compared with the same month a year earlier the CPI was 24.46 percent higher.
The accumulated inflation rate for the first three months of the year was 5.59 percent, compared with 8.35 percent in the same period a year earlier.
It said that the main causes of inflation this year was an increase in prices of automobiles and auto insurance, rent, tomatoes, local telephone service and gasoline.
It said that the basic basket of consumer goods rose 1.19 percent in March from the month before.
Banco de Mexico gave the following breakdown for March:
INDEX Percent
Food, drinks and tobacco 0.69
Clothing and shoes 1.90
Housing 1.41
Furniture 1.40
Health and personal care 1.40
Transportation 1.94
Education 0.72
Other services 1.26
In March, the producer price index, excluding petroleum, was 0.97 percent higher than the same month a year earlier.
Compared to the same month a year earlier, producer prices in March were 20.92 percent higher.
The accumulated increase for the first three months was 4.71 percent, compared to 8.15 percent the same period the year before.
Banco de Mexico said that of the 46 cities where it collects information for the consumer price index, the greatest increases were seen in the following:
CITY CHANGE
Torreon 1.75 pct
Tampico 1.46 pct
